These resources provide background on personalized medicine, treatment-effect prediction and the methods used in **precmed**.

## Handbook

For a broader introduction to personalized medicine using real-world data, see [*Comparative Effectiveness and Personalized Medicine Research Using Real-World Data*](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003300809) [@debray2026comparative]. The following chapters are particularly relevant to **precmed**:

- [Chapter 5](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003300809-5): marginal and conditional treatment effects, including the ATE [@nguyen2026causaleffects].
- [Chapter 17](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003300809-17): principles of CATE prediction and model development in randomized and non-randomized data [@hoogland2026introduction].
- [Chapter 19](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003300809-19): validation strategies and assessment of discrimination, calibration, and decision accuracy [@thao2026validation].
- [Chapter 20](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003300809-20): visualization and interpretation of individualized treatment rules, validation curves, and responder diagnostics, with examples using **precmed** [@jiang2026visualization].

## Free courses

These free courses can help you build the knowledge and practical skills needed to study personalized treatment decisions. [An Introduction to Precision Medicine](https://sdas.thinkific.com/courses/precmedintro) introduces the foundations through recorded webinars, exercises, and readings. The [companion course to the book](https://sdas.thinkific.com/courses/rwd-book) provides background materials, example R code, and curated references to support practical analyses with **precmed** and related methods.

## Methodological references

The original methodological references are @yadlowsky2020estimation for ratio-based CATE estimation and validation, and @zhao2013effectively for target-population selection.
